draft.title: fix(google-drive): prove folder name uniqueness before writes
draft.issueTitle: [Bug]: Incomplete Drive folder-name searches can select the wrong write target
draft.issueBody:
### Details

Name-based folder resolution reads only one files.list page and omits incompleteSearch from its field mask. A later duplicate or an unsearched shared drive can therefore make mkdir, upload, document creation or move choose an unproven parent folder.

## Reproduction

Call the actual makeFolder entry with a parent name. Return a first files.list page with one match, an empty continuation page and a later different folder with the same name. Repeat with one apparent match and incompleteSearch=true. Both should refuse the unproven name before sending any POST. One-page unique names, an explicit folder ID and root are controls.

Reproducible production-entry fixture: https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/blob/afloat16/orca50-20261127-drive-folder-completeness/src/main/google/google-drive-folder-completeness.test.ts

**Before:** Both actual makeFolder regressions wrote a child into the first folder: one despite a duplicate after an empty continuation page, the other despite incompleteSearch=true.

**Expected and verified with the change:** Both uncertain-name operations reject before any POST. A one-page unique name, explicit folder ID and root continue to create children under exactly the requested parent.

Environment: Linux, Node 24.22.3, source checkout 9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817. The provider boundary uses real Response schemas and local protocol fixtures; no live Google account is claimed.

Primary API references:
- https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files/list

**Bounded-search behavior:** Request nextPageToken and incompleteSearch, follow up to 20 pages including empty pages, and stop as soon as the result is complete or distinct matches establish ambiguity. Refuse incompleteSearch or a continuation remaining at the 20-page limit with an explicit-folder-ID remedy; never accept an unproven unique result at the cap. Retain at most five distinct candidate IDs for the ambiguity message.

**Additional boundary evidence:** Manual boundary probe through real GoogleApi and makeFolder: an apparent unique match followed by empty continuing pages and a wholly empty continuing search both stop after 20 pages, return the incomplete-search error and make zero POSTs. A unique match whose search completes exactly on page 20 still creates the child under that folder. Before the cap, the first two probes read page 21 and the apparent unique case performed a POST. The original two committed regressions also pass. The temporary boundary probe is retained in validation only, not committed as a call-count unit test.
draft.prTemplate:
## ELI5

Check enough Drive search pages to prove a folder name is unique, or ask for its ID before writing.

## What Changed

Request nextPageToken and incompleteSearch, follow up to 20 pages including empty pages, and stop as soon as the result is complete or distinct matches establish ambiguity. Refuse incompleteSearch or a continuation remaining at the 20-page limit with an explicit-folder-ID remedy; never accept an unproven unique result at the cap. Retain at most five distinct candidate IDs for the ambiguity message.

## Why

Name-based folder resolution reads only one files.list page and omits incompleteSearch from its field mask. A later duplicate or an unsearched shared drive can therefore make mkdir, upload, document creation or move choose an unproven parent folder.

Production callers: src/main/google/google-drive.ts:makeFolder; src/main/google/google-drive.ts:moveDrive; src/main/google/google-drive.ts:uploadDrive; src/main/google/google-docs.ts:createDoc.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #ISSUE_NUMBER

## Visual Proof

N/A — the change is in CLI/RPC target resolution, with no graphical layout or interaction control change.

| Same production input before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Both actual makeFolder regressions wrote a child into the first folder: one despite a duplicate after an empty continuation page, the other despite incompleteSearch=true. | Both uncertain-name operations reject before any POST. A one-page unique name, explicit folder ID and root continue to create children under exactly the requested parent. |

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally through the actual production entries below
- [x] Automated regression added for external data integrity
- [x] The added regression fails against the original production code and uses the real operation with only provider responses supplied

Call the actual makeFolder entry with a parent name. Return a first files.list page with one match, an empty continuation page and a later different folder with the same name. Repeat with one apparent match and incompleteSearch=true. Both should refuse the unproven name before sending any POST. One-page unique names, an explicit folder ID and root are controls.

```sh
node config/scripts/test-runtime/execution-policy/run-vitest.mjs run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/google/google-drive-folder-completeness.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

Two regressions pass; parent write records remain empty for uncertain names and match the one-page/ID/root control destinations

Manual boundary probe through real GoogleApi and makeFolder: an apparent unique match followed by empty continuing pages and a wholly empty continuing search both stop after 20 pages, return the incomplete-search error and make zero POSTs. A unique match whose search completes exactly on page 20 still creates the child under that folder. Before the cap, the first two probes read page 21 and the apparent unique case performed a POST. The original two committed regressions also pass. The temporary boundary probe is retained in validation only, not committed as a call-count unit test.

Final integrated validation: 32 focused regression tests in 22 files passed, including the unchanged archive-write failure case that had timed out under earlier heavy concurrent checking. The Drive performance contract passed separately (1 file/1 test). Changed-code quality passed with zero new findings across 129 changed paths; final touched-file formatting and git diff --check passed. Node typechecking passed for 17,026 files and web typechecking for 16,094 files using the repository-supported Bun compiler with one worker. These are aggregate validation results for the prepared contributions, not per-PR test counts.

The required `pnpm check:changed --base=9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817` was attempted after the final edits. Its workspace-package build is blocked because this environment rejects the tsx CLI local IPC socket (`listen EPERM`). The default tsrs typechecker was also terminated with SIGKILL; the supported Bun typechecking route completed successfully. The complete gate/build is not claimed to pass and still requires CI.

After the bounded Drive-search follow-up, the two original regressions and a manual page-limit boundary probe passed; changed-code quality again reported zero new findings across 129 paths and Node typechecking again passed for 17,026 files (80.01 s). The required aggregate gate was retried and remains blocked at the same tsx IPC restriction.

Linux was exercised locally. No live Google account, graphical desktop, macOS, Windows or SSH execution is claimed. The provider-neutral code remains on the existing runtime paths.

## Performance

A unique name may require more list reads, capped at 20 pages per name resolution. Retained candidates are capped at five and paging stops as soon as ambiguity is known. No entire folder history is accumulated. A continuation at the cap fails closed before any write. Single-page unique names, direct IDs and root keep their existing resolution. No network write is retried or added.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

Name-based writes may now ask for a folder ID when an all-drives search cannot prove completeness or still has a continuation after 20 pages. That refusal is deliberate and occurs before mutation. Existing explicit IDs and root continue to work. A revert restores prior matching behavior and does not undo files already created.
